text: 13 mg is quite close to the standard naltrexone dosage territory rather than "LDN". With 13 mg you are probably blocking the opioid receptors for most of the day, which is what naltrexone is used for in treating drug/alcohol addiction. At this dosage you wouldn't achieve much of a rebound of endorphins, so in theory this should make you feel worse (most people on standard naltrexone dosage report they feel horrible). Then again naltrexone also works as a microglial inhibitor which modulates the immune system and can reduce pain, maybe this effect gets more prominent at higher dosages. Who know

thread: Does LDN make you tired? If so, did adjusting the dosage help?
parent: what is a microglial inhibitor?
text:
Microglia are special kind of macrophages that are part of the immune defense of the brain and CNS. In CFS/ME it's commonly believed that microglia are in a chronic overactive state, for example many CFS/ME "brain symptoms" such as brain fog could be due to dysfunctioning microglia. LDN works by inhibiting TLR4 receptors of microglia and thus may reduce the excessive microglial activation. You can read more about the theory
here
.
